authority: CEO Round 124 P0 directive: 'World B: Peridigm — 1. install; 2. run official examples; 3. reproduce an analytical tensile/fracture benchmark; 4. establish convergence; 5. certify.'
status: SPECIFICATION — NOT CERTIFICATION. This document specifies HOW Peridigm will be certified. It is NOT a certification. Per Article I (evidence precedes assertion) and Article XXVI (no self-certification), no certification exists until the protocol is executed.

governance_compliance.article_I: Certification is granted only after the corresponding evidence exists. P1 (install) must succeed before P2 (examples) is attempted.
governance_compliance.article_V: Fail closed — a failed P-level BLOCKS all higher P-levels. P3 fail means P4-P8 do not proceed.
governance_compliance.article_VI: Never manufacture provenance — Peridigm version, build hash, dependency versions must be independently verified, not asserted.
governance_compliance.article_VII: A failed P-level is corrected by fixing the install/example/benchmark — never by weakening the acceptance criterion.
governance_compliance.article_VIII: Each P-level includes an adversarial test (intentionally corrupted input, malformed mesh, wrong horizon) that must be REJECTED.
governance_compliance.article_XIV: RED = STOP. A red P-level halts the certification ladder.
governance_compliance.article_XV: Disclosure: any deviation from this protocol during execution MUST be reported honestly, not silently absorbed.
governance_compliance.article_XVII: Each P-level has an attempted bypass — what would make this P-level pass while the underlying system is wrong?
governance_compliance.article_XXVI: Locally verified ≠ CI-certified. Each P-level must be re-runnable from a clean environment by a third party.
governance_compliance.article_XXVII: Every numerical threshold in this protocol has explicit class (PHYSIOLOGICAL / ANALYTICAL / ENGINEERING / MODEL_DERIVED) and provenance.
governance_compliance.article_XXVIII: Passing a P-level grants credit ONLY at that P-level. It does NOT promote to physical validation or to precursor claim support.
governance_compliance.article_XXIX: Implementation failure (Peridigm misconfigured) is separated from mechanism failure (precursor absent).
governance_compliance.article_XXX: Before declaring each P-level GREEN, ask 'what would make this test pass while the underlying system is still wrong?' Then construct the adversarial test.
cemetery_lessons_applied: CE-019 — Do not attribute Peridigm failure to a plausible cause without A/B test.
CE-020 — Material label ≠ constitutive equivalence. Peridigm's 'elastic' material must be matched to FEBio's neo-Hookean by parameter equivalence, not label.
CE-023 — Two implementations can agree and both be wrong. Peridgm agreement with FEBio is necessary but not sufficient.
CE-025 — Three-method verification (analytical + FEBio + Peridigm) catches bugs that two-method cannot.
CE-027 — Derive analytical solutions from source code, not textbook formulas.
CE-029 — Analytical solutions must match Peridigm's boundary conditions, not generic textbook BCs.

independence_argument.code_independence: Peridigm is a separate C++ codebase maintained by Sandia National Laboratories. No shared source with FEBio. No shared author with this project.
independence_argument.discretization_independence: Peridigm uses meshfree discretization (no element connectivity required). FEBio uses FEM (element connectivity required). Fundamentally different numerical methods.
independence_argument.fracture_formulation_independence: Peridigm: fracture emerges from bond breakage between material points. FEBio: fracture imposed via CDM + element deletion (Simo CDF). Different mathematical representations of fracture.
independence_argument.verification_independence: Peridigm has its own test suite (Peridigm/test/). FEBio has its own verification suite. The two suites were authored independently.
independence_argument.attempted_bypass_of_independence_claim: Could Peridgm and FEBio secretly share assumptions? Yes — both could share (a) neo-Hookean material model parameterization, (b) plane-strain assumptions, (c) timestep heuristics. To test: deliberately introduce mismatched material parameterizations and confirm results change predictably. If results do NOT change, the independence claim is weakened.

P1_INSTALLATION.description: Peridigm is installed, builds from source, and the executable runs in a clean environment.
acceptance_criteria: Peridigm builds from source on a clean Linux environment (Ubuntu 22.04+ or equivalent)
All dependencies (Trilinos, MPI, Boost) are at versions specified in Peridigm README
Peridigm executable responds to --help and --version
Build provenance recorded: Peridigm git commit hash, Trilinos version, MPI distribution, compiler version
Docker image built and tagged (Peridigm ships Docker support per audit)
P1_INSTALLATION.adversarial_test: Plant a fake 'peridigm' binary in PATH that silently exits 0. The protocol must detect the substitution (version string mismatch, binary hash mismatch).
P1_INSTALLATION.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Peridigm builds but the wrong version (e.g., a forked branch with non-standard modifications). Mitigation: pin to official master branch at a specific commit, record hash.
P1_INSTALLATION.epistemic_class_on_pass: ENGINEERING — install only; no physics validated yet.

P2_OFFICIAL_EXAMPLES.description: All official Peridigm examples run and produce expected output.
acceptance_criteria: Tensile bar example runs to completion
Fragmentation example (e.g., notched cylinder impact) runs and produces visible fracture pattern
Kalthoff-Winkler impact example runs and crack path matches published pattern
Each example output compared against Peridigm's own test/baseline (regression test)
Output file format (ExodusII) is readable by Paraview
P2_OFFICIAL_EXAMPLES.adversarial_test: Corrupt one input file (e.g., negative Young's modulus). Peridigm must FAIL with a clear error message, not silently produce garbage.
P2_OFFICIAL_EXAMPLES.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Examples pass but Peridigm is using a single CPU silently (MPI broken). Mitigation: verify mpirun -np 4 produces different timing than -np 1 and correct partitioning.
P2_OFFICIAL_EXAMPLES.epistemic_class_on_pass: ENGINEERING — Peridgm's own tests pass; no independent ground truth established yet.

P3_ANALYTICAL_TENSILE_BENCHMARK.description: Reproduce an analytical tensile bar solution. Analogous to FEBio L3 (analytical neo-Hookean verification).
acceptance_criteria: Analytical solution DERIVED FROM Peridigm source code, not textbook (CE-027 lesson). Specifically: derive the constitutive response for the 'Prototypical Peridynamic Material' (or equivalent elastic model) under uniaxial tension.
Analytical solution matches Peridigm boundary conditions (CE-029 lesson). Peridigm uses horizon δ, family of bonds, no fixed nodes in the FEM sense. The analytical solution must reflect this.
Peridgm simulation of tensile bar matches analytical solution to <=1% in stress-strain for small strains (< 10%).
Deviation decreases monotonically with horizon refinement (δ → 0)
Convergence rate matches theoretical prediction (Peridigm should converge to classical continuum in the δ → 0 limit for ordinary state-based)
P3_ANALYTICAL_TENSILE_BENCHMARK.adversarial_test: Use a horizon δ larger than the bar dimension. Peridgm should fail or produce meaningless output — not silently run.
P3_ANALYTICAL_TENSILE_BENCHMARK.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Analytical solution derived incorrectly but happens to match a degenerate Peridgm case. Mitigation: derive analytical solution INDEPENDENTLY (two authors, two methods) before comparison.
P3_ANALYTICAL_TENSILE_BENCHMARK.epistemic_class_on_pass: ANALYTICAL — Peridgm reproduces known continuum mechanics in the small-strain limit. Strong but not fracture-relevant yet.

small_strain_deviation_threshold.justification: 1% is the FEBio L3 acceptance threshold; matched for consistency

convergence_rate_threshold.justification: theoretical prediction; not a numerical threshold

P4_CONVERGENCE_STUDY.description: Establish spatial and temporal convergence for Peridigm on a non-trivial problem (not just tensile bar). Analogous to FEBio L2.
acceptance_criteria: Horizon convergence: δ = {2h, 3h, 4h} with mesh refinement h → 0 at fixed δ/h ratio. Observed convergence rate matches theory.
Mesh convergence: h refined at fixed δ. Convergence to nonlocal solution (not classical continuum).
Time-step convergence: explicit time integration with dt = {0.5*dt_CFL, 0.25*dt_CFL, 0.125*dt_CFL}. Solution stable and convergent.
All three convergence studies on the SAME problem (e.g., Mode I crack propagation in a pre-notched plate).
Results plotted with error bars and convergence rates reported with confidence intervals
P4_CONVERGENCE_STUDY.adversarial_test: Run with dt > dt_CFL (CFL violation). Peridigm should produce unstable results (energy non-conservation), not silently damp.
P4_CONVERGENCE_STUDY.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Convergence appears OK because the problem is too easy (linear elastic, no fracture). Mitigation: include fracture in the convergence problem (pre-notched plate with crack growth).
P4_CONVERGENCE_STUDY.epistemic_class_on_pass: ANALYTICAL + NUMERICAL — Peridgm's numerical machinery is verified.

P5_FRACTURE_BENCHMARK.description: Reproduce a published analytical or experimental fracture benchmark. This is where Peridgm's fracture formulation is independently validated.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark: Kalthoff-Winkler impact experiment (peridynamics' canonical fracture benchmark).
Crack propagation angle matches published experimental value (~70° from impact direction) within ±5°.
Crack speed matches published experimental value within ±20%.
OR: Mode I crack propagation in pre-notched plate. Stress intensity factor matches analytical (LEFM) prediction within ±5% in small-scale yielding regime.
Result is reproducible across multiple mesh refinements (not a single-mesh artifact).
P5_FRACTURE_BENCHMARK.adversarial_test: Set bond-failure threshold to a value that would prevent any fracture. Peridgm should produce elastic response with no cracks — not silently introduce numerical fracture.
P5_FRACTURE_BENCHMARK.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Crack angle matches because of mesh-bias (pre-notched plate with mesh aligned to expected crack path). Mitigation: use UNALIGNED mesh or random mesh perturbation.
P5_FRACTURE_BENCHMARK.epistemic_class_on_pass: ANALYTICAL + EXPERIMENTAL — Peridgm's fracture formulation is validated against published physical data.

crack_speed_tolerance.justification: experimental crack speed measurements vary widely

P6_INDEPENDENT_PUBLISHED_DATA_REPRODUCTI.description: Reproduce a published computational result that uses peridynamics for a biological/soft-tissue problem. This bridges Peridgm from hard-materials fracture to soft-tissue biomechanics.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark: 2026 CFD+peridynamics thrombus embolization paper (PubMed 42367319) — see VIRTUAL_LAB_BENCHMARK_1_SPEC.json
Reproduce the published embolization timing within ±15% of reported value
Reproduce the published fragment size distribution within Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance 0.2
Reproduce the published threshold pressure for embolization onset within ±20%
All material parameters sourced from the published paper, not re-fit
P6_INDEPENDENT_PUBLISHED_DATA_REPRODUCTI.adversarial_test: Use parameters OUTSIDE the published range (e.g., 10x stiffer clot). Peridgm should produce qualitatively different behavior (no embolization or much higher threshold) — not silently reproduce the published result.
P6_INDEPENDENT_PUBLISHED_DATA_REPRODUCTI.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Reproduction succeeds because of overfitting (re-fit parameters under the guise of 'calibration'). Mitigation: parameters from the paper, no re-fit. If reproduction fails with paper parameters, FAIL P6 — do not re-fit.
P6_INDEPENDENT_PUBLISHED_DATA_REPRODUCTI.epistemic_class_on_pass: EXPERIMENTAL — Peridgm reproduces published biological/soft-tissue fracture data. This is the gateway to using Peridgm for the precursor.

embolization_timing_tolerance.justification: computational reproduction tolerance; smaller than experimental variation

ks_distance_fragment_distribution.justification: standard KS distance for distributional similarity

P7_CROSS_WORLD_COMPARISON.description: Run the SAME simplified clot-loading benchmark in BOTH FEBio and Peridgm. Compare results. This is the FIRST point at which multi-simulator cross-validation becomes meaningful.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark: simplified clot cylinder under uniaxial compression, with damage/fracture allowed. Same geometry, same loading, same material parameters (where constitutive equivalence is meaningful).
Force-displacement curve compared between FEBio and Peridgm in the pre-failure regime. Required: <=5% deviation in stiffness, <=10% deviation in peak force.
Failure mode compared qualitatively. Both should show damage localization in the same region (or document disagreement and explain).
Disagreement, if any, is CLASSIFIED per the simulator_disagreement_classification (PHYSICS_DISAGREEMENT / MATHEMATICAL_MODEL_DISAGREEMENT / etc.) — NOT automatically promoted to HYPOTHESIS_KILLED.

The disagreement classification is supported by A/B testing (CE-019 lesson) — e.g., if disagreement is attributed to CDM vs. bond-breakage, run Peridgm with a CDM-like correspondence model to test the attribution.
P7_CROSS_WORLD_COMPARISON.adversarial_test: Run FEBio and Peridgm with deliberately mismatched material parameters (e.g., 2x stiffer in Peridgm). Both should produce different results — not silently agree. If they agree despite parameter mismatch, the comparison is meaningless.
P7_CROSS_WORLD_COMPARISON.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Forced agreement by re-parameterizing one simulator to match the other post-hoc. Mitigation: parameters set INDEPENDENTLY from material characterization, not re-fit to each other.
P7_CROSS_WORLD_COMPARISON.epistemic_class_on_pass: ANALYTICAL + EXPERIMENTAL — cross-simulator agreement (or classified disagreement) on a simplified problem.

peak_force_deviation_threshold.justification: wider than stiffness due to fracture sensitivity

P8_INDEPENDENCE_CERTIFICATION.description: Formal certification that Peridgm satisfies the independence requirements for cross-validation. Without this, P7 results cannot be claimed as 'multi-simulator validation.'
acceptance_criteria: Code independence: Peridgm git commit hash != FEBio git commit hash; no shared source files
Discretization independence: meshfree vs. FEM (documented)
Fracture formulation independence: bond breakage vs. CDM + element deletion (documented)
Author independence: Peridigm developers != FEBio developers != this project's authors (verified by author metadata in source repositories)
Benchmark independence: Peridigm test suite != FEBio verification suite (verified by file-level comparison)

Constitutive equivalence: where Peridgm and FEBio use the SAME material model (e.g., neo-Hookean in correspondence formulation), parameters are matched by ANALYTICAL EQUIVALENCE, not label (CE-020 lesson). The 1/J factor error (CE-023 lesson) is checked.
All independence claims VERIFIED BY FILE-LEVEL COMPARISON, not asserted.
P8_INDEPENDENCE_CERTIFICATION.adversarial_test: For each independence claim, ask: 'What shared assumption could Peridgm and FEBio secretly have?' Test by deliberately violating the assumption and confirming results change.
P8_INDEPENDENCE_CERTIFICATION.what_would_make_this_pass_while_wrong: Independence claimed but Peridgm secretly imported FEBio's material model. Mitigation: file-level grep for shared code, parameter-file structural comparison.
P8_INDEPENDENCE_CERTIFICATION.epistemic_class_on_pass: INDEPENDENCE_CERTIFIED — Peridgm is genuinely independent of FEBio. Cross-simulator comparison is now MEANINGFUL.

ladder_invariants.no_skipping: P-levels may not be skipped. P3 requires P2 GREEN. P4 requires P3 GREEN. Etc.
ladder_invariants.no_retroactive_amendment: Once a P-level is GREEN, its acceptance criteria may not be retroactively weakened. If a higher P-level reveals a P-level bug, the lower P-level is RE-CERTIFIED, not grandfathered.
ladder_invariants.no_self_certification: P-levels must be verified by running the protocol in a clean environment, not by the agent who installed Peridgm. CI artifact required.
ladder_invariants.evidence_custody: Each P-level pass produces an artifact (log, plot, output file) committed to the repository with provenance (Peridigm version, input file, output hash, commit hash).
ladder_invariants.honest_failure: If any P-level fails, the failure is recorded with the failure mode, the suspected cause, and the A/B test that would confirm or refute the cause (CE-019).

what_this_protocol_does_NOT_certify.not_clot_physics: P1-P8 certify Peridgm as a peridynamics solver. They do NOT certify that peridynamics is the right physics for clots. That requires the precursor test (after P8).
what_this_protocol_does_NOT_certify.not_precursor_existence: P1-P8 do NOT test whether the precursor exists in Peridgm. That is the next phase after certification.
what_this_protocol_does_NOT_certify.not_physical_validation: P1-P8 are virtual certification. They do NOT replace physical experiment (E4/E5).
what_this_protocol_does_NOT_certify.not_replacement_for_FEBio: Peridgm is INDEPENDENT of FEBio, not a REPLACEMENT. FEBio remains the validated L1-L8 stack. Peridgm adds an independent cross-validation universe.

honest_status: SPECIFICATION ONLY. Zero P-levels executed. Peridgm not installed. No certification exists. This protocol is the design artifact; execution is the next phase.
